**Things on EKS that only exist for EKS:** the gp3 default StorageClass
(`k8s/storage/`, EKS ships none), the EBS CSI driver and Karpenter (IAM in Terraform,
controller and `k8s/karpenter/` NodePools via Argo CD), control plane ServiceMonitors
disabled in the Prometheus values. vLLM's
Deployment has no `replicas` and its Application ignores `/spec/replicas`, because KEDA
owns the count; adding `replicas` back would make self-heal undo every scale-to-zero.
Teardown must go through `scripts/teardown-eks.sh` before `terraform destroy`:
Karpenter's instances aren't Terraform resources, so the script deletes the NodePools
first (with root's auto-sync off, or Argo CD recreates them) and waits for the nodes
to go while Karpenter still runs; destroying with PVCs still present orphans their EBS
volumes. Both keep billing.

[1] docs/retrieval-eval.md - In CI
## In CI

The `rag-image` job runs the evaluation on the image it just built (its
model, chunking and docs), before scanning and publishing it, and fails if
any metric drops below `apps/rag/eval/baseline.json`:

| Minimum | Measured |
|---|---|
| all hit@k 0.83 | 0.857 (48 of 56) |
| all MRR 0.72 | 0.743 |
| English hit@k 0.84 | 0.867 (39 of 45) |
| Spanish hit@k 0.72 | 0.818 (9 of 11) |

Measured with 0.2.5 on the 66-question set and the docs as of the seventh
EKS run. When the baseline was first set (0.2.0), adding this document to the
corpus moved MRR from 0.694 to 0.672 (it outranked the source passage for a
few questions about the RAG service) without changing hit@k. Each minimum
lets one question slip: the corpus is the docs themselves, so every doc
change re-ranks a little. Raise them when retrieval improves. The full
per-question table goes to the job summary. It takes ~40 s on a laptop's 2 CPUs.

[2] docs/retrieval-eval.md - In CI

Locally, with the image built (`docker build -f apps/rag/Dockerfile -t
llm-platform-rag:dev .`):

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/apps/rag/eval":/eval:ro llm-platform-rag:dev \
  python -m rag.evaluate --questions /eval/questions.yaml --baseline /eval/baseline.json
```

`EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `QUERY_PREFIX`, `DOCUMENT_PREFIX`, `CHUNK_SIZE` and
`CHUNK_OVERLAP` are environment variables, so a candidate configuration can
be evaluated without code changes (a model other than the baked one needs
its cache mounted at `/models`, or `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0` to download it).

[3] docs/cost-comparison.md - Fourth run (2026-10-20): RAG service and signed images
gestion**: 60 chunks in 18 s on a platform node (it took minutes on the
8 GB laptop, starved by the rest of the local stack).

Bugs found on this run:

- **Ingestion OOMKilled** under its 768 MiB limit: ONNX memory grows with the
  batch (peak 834 MiB at 32 chunks per call, 452 MiB at 8). Batch now 8.
- **A failing Sync hook blocks newer revisions**: the ingestion Job is an
  Argo CD Sync hook, and while it kept failing on 0.1.0 the sync operation
  stayed Running on the old revision, so the fixed 0.1.1 commit wasn't picked
  up until the operation was terminated by hand. The failed attempts left 12
  half-built collections; the next successful ingestion removed them all.
- **Mistral's chat template rejects a system message** (400 from vLLM); the
  local Ollama mock accepted it. The prompt is now a single user message.
- **claude-fallback rejected `temperature=0`** (claude-sonnet-5 only accepts
  1), for any gateway client: LiteLLM now drops unsupported parameters
  (`drop_params`). LiteLLM only reads its ConfigMap at startup, so the change
  needed a manual rollout restart.

[4] docs/retrieval-eval.md - Method
## Method

`python -m rag.evaluate` (`apps/rag/rag/evaluate.py`) indexes the image's own
corpus (README, CLAUDE.md, docs/) into an in-memory Qdrant with the same
chunking and embeddings as the ingestion Job, then searches every question in
`apps/rag/eval/questions.yaml`:

- **56 answerable questions** (45 English, 11 Spanish), each with `evidence`:
  text that must appear in a retrieved chunk for it to count as a hit.
  Evidence is matched against chunk text rather than chunk ids, so changing
  the chunking doesn't invalidate the set; if a doc edit removes an evidence
  string, the evaluator fails and names the question to update.
- **10 unanswerable questions**, scored on similarity only: off-topic ones
  (capital of France, today's date, ...) and technical ones close to the
  corpus's vocabulary but not about this platform (OpenAI's API price,
  Kubernetes on a Raspberry Pi).

*Sustained traffic with enough concurrency to batch:** keeping the GPU
  warm pays off, and spot capacity roughly halves the cost when it's available.

Where the line falls between the two depends on the external provider's
current per-token pricing and on your own traffic. The Grafana dashboard
`k8s/observability/grafana-dashboard-llm-cost.yaml` computes both sides live:
set the provider's API prices and the GPU node's hourly cost in its variables.

**Autoscaling and observability share one Prometheus install.** KEDA's
`ScaledObject` (`k8s/vllm/keda-scaledobject.yaml`) queries the same
kube-prometheus-stack Prometheus (`k8s/observability/prometheus-grafana-values.yaml`,
release name `prometheus`) that scrapes cost/latency metrics via the
`ServiceMonitor`s in `k8s/observability/servicemonitors.yaml`. vLLM exposes native
Prometheus metrics; LiteLLM needs `litellm_settings.success_callback`/
`failure_callback: ["prometheus"]` set to expose its `/metrics` endpoint — this is
what feeds `docs/cost-comparison.md`. OpenCost (infra-side cost) is not installed
anywhere yet — it only appears as a documented next step in the comments at the end
of `prometheus-grafana-values.yaml`.

**Tracing (Tempo, `rag/tracing.py`).** On EKS the RAG API and LiteLLM send
OpenTelemetry spans over OTLP/HTTP to Tempo (`k8s/argocd/apps/tempo.yaml`,
single binary, no persistent volume, 24 h retention), a Grafana datasource. One
question is one trace: FastAPI's native telemetry opens the request span,
`rag.ask` and its `rag.embed`/`rag.retrieve`/`rag.generate` stages hang under it
(scores, sources, model, token counts as attributes), and LiteLLM's spans hang
under `rag.generate` because the API injects a `traceparent` into the model call.
`/healthz` and `/metrics` are excluded. Tracing is off whenever
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is unset (unit tests, CI's evaluation, kind, where
`deploy-local.sh` strips it). LiteLLM's spans include the full prompt. The Tempo
chart lives in grafana-community/helm-charts (deprecated in grafana/helm-charts). Measured results:
docs/tracing.md.

[4] docs/cost-comparison.md - Third run (2026-10-14): Karpenter, image cache that works
## Third run (2026-10-14): Karpenter, image cache that works

GPU nodes now come from Karpenter (`k8s/karpenter/`) instead of a managed
node group + Cluster Autoscaler. Karpenter builds each launch from the
EC2NodeClass, so the data volume's provisioned initialization rate actually
reaches EC2 (verified on the volume: `InitializationType: provisioned-rate`,
300 MiB/s, 100% before vLLM needed it). Same measurement script, single
request, from zero vLLM pods and zero GPU nodes:

| | Karpenter, no cache | Karpenter + snapshot (1) | Karpenter + snapshot (2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| KEDA sees the request | 41 s | 45 s | 22 s |
| Karpenter decides (NodeClaim) | +12 s | +12 s | +11 s |
| EC2 node object | +19 s | +32 s | +24 s |
| Node Ready | +15 s | +14 s | +13 s |
| Image pull | 4:41 | 0 (on disk) | 0 (on disk) |
| Container start → vLLM Ready | 4:44 | 3:43 | 3:34 |
| **Request → first vLLM answer** | **~11 min** | **5:43** | **5:14** |

[1] docs/retrieval-eval.md - Similarity threshold: ruled out
## Similarity threshold: ruled out

The idea from the fourth run was to skip the model call when the best chunk
scores too low. With bge-small, an unanswerable question outscored a real hit
(separation -0.069): any threshold drops right answers. With embeddinggemma
the gap is +0.010 (best unanswerable 0.256, weakest hit 0.266): technically
separable, but too thin to trust on 5 unanswerable questions, and it didn't
survive adding this document to the corpus (-0.043: a weak hit's best chunk
is now this page).

[2] docs/retrieval-eval.md - Results
## Results

All on the original 35 questions and the corpus at the time, CHUNK_SIZE 1000
unless noted.

| Embedding model | hit@1 | hit@4 | MRR | Spanish hit@4 | Separation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (before) | 0.50 | 0.70 | 0.59 | 0.40 | -0.069 |
| bge-small, CHUNK_SIZE 500 | worse | | | | |
| bge-small, its query instruction | same as plain | | | | |
| paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2 | worse | | | | |
| potion-multilingual-128m | worse | | | | |
| google/embeddinggemma-300m, no prompts | 0.53 | 0.87 | 0.67 | 1.00 | -0.040 |
| **embeddinggemma-300m with task prompts (now)** | **0.57** | **0.90** | **0.69** | **0.80** | **+0.010** |

embeddinggemma is trained with task prompts, prepended here as

cost of one Spanish question (1.00 -> 0.80).

The larger set settled it: an unanswerable question about the platform's
own topic scores like a real match. "How much does the OpenAI API cost per
million tokens?" scores 0.52, higher than the best chunk of 29 of the 48
questions retrieval gets right, and "How do I install Kubernetes on a
Raspberry Pi?" 0.47, higher than 16. Off-topic questions stay at 0.10-0.27.
A similarity threshold would only catch the questions that were never the
problem, so there won't be one: declining is the model's job (the judge's
`declines` check).
